body.statement: For every law \(P\) for which the reduced-form primitives are defined, the sharp identified set is the always-defined sublevel set \(\Theta_I(P)=\{\theta\in K:q_P(\theta)\leq0\}\). If \(\delta(P)<0\), then \(\Theta_I(P)=\varnothing\). If \(\delta(P)\geq0\), the raw analytic endpoints \(\theta_-(P)\) and \(\theta_+(P)\) are real-valued and \(\Theta_I(P)=K\cap[\theta_-(P),\theta_+(P)]\). For every \(P\in\mathcal P_W\), the structural equations and \(L_2\) leakage restriction give \(\alpha(P)-\theta_0\beta(P)=\gamma\) and hence \(\theta_0\in\Theta_I(P)\). Therefore the parameter-margin condition forces \(\theta_-(P),\theta_+(P)\in\operatorname{int}(K)\), so \(\Theta_I(P)=[\theta_-(P),\theta_+(P)]\), for every \(P\in\mathcal P_n^{\mathrm{ct}}(C_{\delta})\cup\mathcal P^{\mathrm{int}}(\delta_0)\); no \(K\)-truncation occurs on either maintained regime.
body.justification: The lemma gives the raw square-root formulas their exact domain and shows that the maintained margin condition removes parameter-space truncation wherever endpoint asymptotics are used.
body.gap: Watson et al. give the quadratic reduction, but the contact analysis requires an explicit distinction between the globally defined sublevel set and partial raw endpoints.
body.consumer: All endpoint limits and lower-bound paths can invoke raw endpoints without evaluating a square root at negative slack or silently dropping the intersection with \(K\).
body.proof_tex:
Put \(b=\|\beta(P)\|_2\), \(c=\check\theta(P)\), and
\[
 r=\alpha(P)-c\beta(P).
\]
The phrase \emph{the reduced-form primitives are defined} includes \(b>0\), because the displayed definition of \(\check\theta(P)\) divides by \(b^2\).  That definition gives \(\beta(P)^{\prime}r=0\).  Consequently, by the Pythagorean identity,
\[
 \begin{split}
 q_P(\theta)
 &=\|r+(c-\theta)\beta(P)\|_2^2-\tau^2\\
 &=\|r\|_2^2+b^2(\theta-c)^2-\tau^2
 =b^2(\theta-c)^2-\delta(P). \tag{1}
 \end{split}
\]
The published reduction in \(\mathrm{def:watson\mbox{-}published\mbox{-}reduction}\) identifies the causal target with the observed-law sublevel set in (1); thus this equality is not imposed by definition in the present proof.  If \(\delta(P)<0\), (1) is strictly positive for every real \(\theta\), and hence \(\Theta_I(P)=\varnothing\).  If \(\delta(P)\geq0\), division by \(b>0\) in (1) gives
\[
 q_P(\theta)\leq0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 c-\frac{\sqrt{\delta(P)}}{b}\leq\theta\leq
 c+\frac{\sqrt{\delta(P)}}{b}.
\]
The two endpoints are exactly \(\theta_-(P)\) and \(\theta_+(P)\), so
\[
 \Theta_I(P)=K\cap[\theta_-(P),\theta_+(P)]. \tag{2}
\]
Now let \(P\in\mathcal P_W\).  Premultiplying the outcome equation in \(\mathrm{ass:outcome\mbox{-}equation}\) by \(Z_i\), taking expectations, and using \(\mathrm{ass:outcome\mbox{-}orthogonality}\) gives
\[
 \Sigma_{zy}(P)=\Sigma_{zz}(P)\gamma+\theta_0\Sigma_{zx}(P).
\]
The covariance-conditioning assumption makes \(\Sigma_{zz}(P)\) invertible.  Applying its inverse and the definitions of \(\alpha(P)\) and \(\beta(P)\) yields
\[
 \alpha(P)-\theta_0\beta(P)=\gamma. \tag{3}
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:l2\mbox{-}leakage}\), (3) implies \(q_P(\theta_0)=\|\gamma\|_2^2-\tau^2\leq0\).  Because \(\theta_0\in K\), the structural target belongs to \(\Theta_I(P)\); in particular the set is nonempty and \(\delta(P)\geq0\).

Write \(K=[k_-,k_+]\).  If \(\theta_-(P)\leq k_-\), then (2) and nonemptiness imply \(k_-\in\Theta_I(P)\), so \(\operatorname{dist}(\Theta_I(P),\partial K)=0\), contrary to \(\mathrm{ass:parameter\mbox{-}margin}\).  Hence \(\theta_-(P)>k_-\).  The same argument at the right boundary gives \(\theta_+(P)<k_+\).  Therefore (2) has no truncation and
\[
 \Theta_I(P)=[\theta_-(P),\theta_+(P)].
\]
Both the contact class and the interior class are subclasses of \(\mathcal P_W\), so the conclusion applies on their union.
